title: Weight detection by trace energy
statement:
Let $N\ne0$ be pure of weight $v$ and lisse on a smooth geometrically
connected affine curve $V_0$. Put

$$
S_n(V_0,N)=\sum_{x\in V_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}
|\iota\Tr(\DLAFr_x\mid N_{\bar x})|^2,
$$

where $\DLAFr_x$ means Frobenius relative to $\mathbf F_{q^n}$.
If $S_n(V_0,N)\le Cq^{nB}$ for every $n\ge1$, with a constant $C>0$
independent of $n$, then $v\le B-1$.

proof.text: Write $V=V_0\times_{k_0}k$. Work in the rational $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil category of the setup; a Weil automorphism is not required to preserve an integral lattice. Choose $b\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ with $\iota(b)=q^v$, possible since $\iota$ is a field isomorphism and $q^v>0$. The constant Weil line $T_v=\mathcal B_b$ is defined by $g\mapsto b^{\deg(g)}$. Use the lisse sheaf--representation tensor equivalence and the contragredient action to form the lisse sheaves $N^c=N^\vee\otimes T_v$ and $D=N\otimes N^c$. The dual is lisse by [lem-tw-dual-stalk-frobenius], and tensoring finite-dimensional representations preserves lisseness under that equivalence.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: construction of the conjugate twist

proof.text:
At a closed point $x$ of degree $d$, write $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ for the realized local eigenvalues of $N$. By purity $|a_i|^2=q^{dv}$ and $a_i\ne0$. The contragredient and tensor spectra of [p-linear-spectra], the constant-line action, and the stalk/representation polynomial comparison give the local eigenvalues $q^{dv}/a_i=\overline{a_i}$ on $N^c$ and $a_i\overline{a_j}$ on $D$. Thus $T_v,N^c,D$ have weights $2v,v,2v$, respectively. If $y\in V_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ lies above $x$, with $n=dm$, [lem-zl-weil-constant-extension-frobenius] identifies its Frobenius with $F_x^m$ up to conjugacy. A triangular basis from [p-linear-triangular] gives eigenvalues $a_i^m$ and $\overline{a_j}^m$, so the diagonal entries of the tensor matrix sum to
$$\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y^{(n)}\mid D_{\bar y})=\sum_{i,j}a_i^m\overline{a_j}^m=\left|\sum_i a_i^m\right|^2=|\iota t_{N,n}(y)|^2.$$
The double sum, including the terms with $i\ne j$, is essential. No semisimplicity of Frobenius is used.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: local spectra, purity and squared traces

proof.text: Apply [sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints] with $C_0=U_0=V_0$, $j=\operatorname{id}$ and $F=D$. Its hypotheses hold because $V_0$ is smooth, geometrically connected and affine and $D$ is lisse. It gives $H_c^0(V,D)=0$, no compact cohomology outside $0,1,2$, and purity of $H_c^2(V,D)$ of weight $2v+2$ (including the possibility that this group is zero). By [prop-cohomological-finiteness], computed at a finite coefficient stage $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ over which $D$ and its Weil structure are defined (the common-stage category of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]), these groups are finite-dimensional with Frobenius automorphisms. Put $A(T)=\iota\det(1-TF_q\mid H_c^1(V,D))$ and $B_2(T)=\iota\det(1-TF_q\mid H_c^2(V,D))$. Both have constant coefficient $1$.

source.place: Proof, first and last paragraphs: endpoint vanishing and degree-two purity

proof.text:
The sums over rational points are finite by [lem-weil-point-counts-finite]. Apply the assumed trace formula [nt-assume-trace-formula] to $D$, in degree zero, with model Frobenius the $q$-power relative Frobenius of $V$: $V_0$ is affine, hence separated of finite type; the fixed points of its $n$-th power are $V_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, finite; $R\Gamma_c(V,D)$ and the stalks are dualizable by step 3. Clause (4) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] turns both categorical traces into alternating sums of ordinary traces; then apply $\iota$. Step 2 identifies the left side with $S_n$, and step 3 reduces the right side to $-\operatorname{Tr}(F_q^n\mid H_c^1)+\operatorname{Tr}(F_q^n\mid H_c^2)$. With [lem-zl-euler-product-identity] for $H_c^1,H_c^2$, [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] and [lem-weil-exp-coefficientwise-map] for $\iota$,
$$U(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{S_n}{n}T^n,\qquad E(T)=\exp U(T)=\frac{A(T)}{B_2(T)}$$
in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: trace formula and determinant identity

proof.text: There is a closed point $x$ of $V_0$: it is nonempty, quasi-compact and Kolmogorov [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point]. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], its degree $d$ is finite and positive. The stalk of $N$ at any geometric point over $x$ is nonzero, since the fibre equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations] on the connected geometric curve reflects zero objects and $N\ne0$. Let $F_x$ be its Frobenius automorphism. If $\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^m)=0$ for every $m\ge1$, [lem-zl-euler-product-identity], applied to the Frobenius module $(N_{\bar x},F_x)$, gives $\det(1-TF_x)^{-1}=\exp(0)=1$. This is impossible: triangularize $F_x$ by [p-linear-triangular]; on a positive-dimensional space its nonzero diagonal eigenvalues give a determinant polynomial of positive degree. Hence some $\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^m)$ is nonzero. The point $x$ lifts to $\mathbf F_{q^{dm}}$, and [lem-zl-weil-constant-extension-frobenius] identifies its local operator with $F_x^m$. Thus $S_{dm}>0$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: a positive energy coefficient

proof.text:
Every $S_n\ge0$ by its definition as a finite sum of squared absolute values. Choose $k\ge1$ with $S_k>0$ from step 5. The coefficient formula of [def-weil-power-series-exponential] expresses every coefficient of $E$ as a sum of nonnegative terms. For every $r\ge1$, its term with $r$ indices all equal to $k$ gives
$$[T^{rk}]E\ \ge\ \frac{(S_k/k)^r}{r!}>0.$$
Thus $E$ has infinitely many nonzero coefficients and cannot be a polynomial.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: positivity prevents a polynomial exponential

proof.text: Reduce the nonzero rational function $A/B_2$ to $P/Q$ by cancelling its polynomial gcd, as in [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Since $A(0)=B_2(0)=1$, the common divisor has nonzero value at $0$, $Q(0)\ne0$, and $QE=P$ as formal series. Step 6 forces $\deg Q>0$, since a constant $Q$ would make $E=P/Q$ a polynomial. The fundamental theorem of algebra [lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed] supplies a root $z$ of $Q$. Coprimality of $P,Q$ gives $P(z)\ne0$: otherwise $T-z$ divides both. Thus $z$ is one surviving denominator root; no assertion that all denominator roots survive is needed.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: one surviving finite pole

proof.text:
Triangularize Frobenius on $H_c^2(V,D)$ using [p-linear-triangular], and apply [p-linear-filtration] to its invariant flag. If $\lambda_j$ are its realized eigenvalues, then
$$B_2(T)=\prod_j(1-\lambda_jT),\qquad |\lambda_j|=q^{v+1}$$
by the purity from step 3 and the weight convention [sk-d-dl-a1-setup]. Since $Q$ divides $B_2$ up to a nonzero constant, the root $z$ of step 7 is $\lambda_j^{-1}$ for some $j$. Hence $|z|=q^{-(v+1)}$. If $H_c^2=0$, then $B_2=1$ and step 7 is already impossible; the same argument excludes this case without assuming it away.

Set $R=q^{-B}>0$. For $0\le t<R$ and $n\ge1$, the assumed bound gives
$$0\le \frac{S_n}{n}t^n\le C(q^Bt)^n.$$
The geometric ratio $q^Bt$ lies in $[0,1)$; its partial sums are bounded by $(1-q^Bt)^{-1}$. The comparison [lem-rp-nonnegative-summable-comparison] therefore gives absolute convergence of $U$ at every such $t$. In the radius convention [d-real-series], $R(U)\ge q^{-B}$. Apply [lem-dl-a1-formal-exponential-radius] to $U$, whose constant coefficient is zero, to obtain $R(E)\ge R(U)\ge q^{-B}$.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: the assumed energy bound gives convergence on the disk

proof.text:
Apply [lem-wf-rational-series-pole-radius] to $QE=P$ and the root $z$ constructed in step 7; it requires precisely $Q(0)\ne0$, $Q(z)=0$ and $P(z)\ne0$, all verified there. Steps 8 and 9 give
$$q^{-B}\le R(E)\le |z|=q^{-(v+1)}.$$
Since $q>1$, the real function $a\mapsto q^a$ is strictly increasing, so $-B\le-(v+1)$ and $v\le B-1$. The argument imposes no weight bound on $H_c^1$.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: exclude the surviving pole from the convergence disk

tool_uses.why: Identifies stalk Frobenius polynomials with the representation operators so dual and tensor spectra compute local eigenvalues; a generic interface, not an alternate purity argument.
Identifies rational-point Frobenius over a constant extension with a power of closed-point Frobenius, without requiring an integral invariant lattice; generic local-operator compatibility.
Supplies lisseness of the dual and the contragredient stalk operator; generic lisse linear-dual compatibility.
Gives a closed point of the nonempty finite-type curve, a generic topological existence tool not supplied by an energy-specific node.
Makes the closed-point residue field finite over the base, allowing a rational-point contribution at a positive extension degree.
Its fibre equivalence on a connected curve reflects zero objects, so every geometric stalk of a nonzero lisse sheaf is nonzero.
Generic comparison of nonnegative numerical series proves convergence under the explicit geometric majorant; it does not replace any sheaf-theoretic step.
Finite-dimensionality of H_c^i(V,D), needed for the determinants A,B_2 and for the dualizability hypothesis of the assumed trace formula; batch-5 permitted finiteness input.

Clause (4) only: over a coefficient field the categorical trace is the alternating sum of traces on cohomology, which the assumed trace formula explicitly leaves out of its scope; a general trace law, not a step of the trace formula.
exp(U+W)=exp(U)exp(W) and exp(-U)=exp(U)^{-1} combine the degree-1 and degree-2 log-det identities; generic formal-series algebra.

lean.statement:
theorem le_sub_one_of_traceEnergy_le (ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ) {V : Scheme.{u}}
    [V.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine V]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (V ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [GeometricallyConnected (V ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    (N : WeilSheaf k₀ l V) (hN : ¬ Limits.IsZero N) (hlisse : N.IsLisse) {v : ℝ}
    (hpure : N.IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight ι v) {C B : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C)
    (hS : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → N.traceEnergy ι n ≤ C * (Nat.card k₀ : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) * B)) :
    v ≤ B - 1
lean.note: Exact existing trace-energy definition and weight-detection statement, both explicitly tagged sk-l-dl-a1-energy upstream. The finite field has cardinality Nat.card k₀; the trace uses geometric Frobenius relative to the extension degree. SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1, geometric connectedness and affineness encode the smooth geometrically connected affine curve. No duplicate module; this stage-2 attachment does not claim a sorry-free upstream proof.
